After two days, on the third day, which is his glorious resurrection, he received him from earth into the heavens — whence the very Spirit had come to the virgin, whose neither birth nor passion the Jews acknowledged. Therefore, since the Jews still contend that Christ has not yet come, whom in so many ways we have proved to have come, let the Jews recognize their own outcome, which they were foretold as about to undergo after the coming of Christ, for the impiety by which they both despised and slew him. For first, from the day on which, according to the saying of Isaiah, a man cast away his abominations of gold and silver, which they made for adoring vanities and harmful things — that is, from the time when we the nations, our hearts being enlightened through the truth of Christ, cast away the idols (let the Jews see) — what follows has been struck out. For the Lord of hosts took away from among the Jews and from Jerusalem, among other things, also the wise architect, who builds the church of God, the temple, and the holy city, and the house of the Lord. For from then the grace of God ceased among them. And it was commanded to the clouds that they should not rain rain upon the vineyard of Soreq — that is, the heavenly benefits — that they should not come to the house of Israel. For it had made thorns, from which it had crowned Christ, and not justice, but the outcry by which it had forced him onto the cross. And so, the former gifts being withdrawn, the law and the prophets were until John; and the pool of Bethesda was until the coming of Christ. He ceased thereafter to cure the diseases of Israel, when from the persistence of their madness the name of the Lord was blasphemed through them, as it is written: Because of you the name of God is blasphemed among the nations. For from them the infamy began; and the middle time was from Tiberius to Vespasian. And since they had committed these things, and had not understood that Christ was to be found in the time of their visitation, their land was made deserted, and their cities burned with fire; strangers devouring their region before their face, the daughter of Zion was left like a watch-post in a vineyard, or like a hut in a cucumber field — that is, from the time when Israel did not know the Lord, and the people did not understand him, but rather forsook him and provoked the Holy One of Israel to indignation. So too the conditional threat of the sword: If you will not, nor obey, the sword shall devour you. From which we prove that the sword was Christ, by not hearing whom they perished — who in the psalm too asks of the Father their dispersion, saying: Scatter them in your power. Who again, through Isaiah, prays for their burning: Because of me, he says, these things have been done to you; in anguish you shall sleep. Since, then, these things were foretold as about to be suffered by the Jews on account of Christ, and we find that they have suffered them, and see them lingering in dispersion, it is plain that these things befell the Jews on account of Christ, the sense of the Scriptures conspiring with the outcome of events and the order of the times. Or if Christ has not yet come, on account of whom they were foretold as about to suffer these things, then when he has come, they shall suffer them. And where then is the daughter of Zion to be left, who today is nothing? where are the cities to be burned, which are already burned and lie in mounds? where is the dispersion of the nation, which is already an exile? Restore the state of Judaea, which Christ may find, and then contend that another is to come.

Learn now, from the abundance of your error, its leadership. We say that two characters of Christ were shown by the prophets, and as many comings of his marked beforehand. One in humility, the first, of course, when he had to be led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer, voiceless, so he opened not his mouth — not even comely to look upon. For we have announced, he says, concerning him, like a little child, like a root in thirsty ground, and he had neither form nor glory. And we saw him, and he had no form nor beauty, but his form was without honour, failing beyond the sons of men, a man in affliction, and knowing how to bear weakness — namely, as set by the Father for a stone of offence, and made by him a little lower than the angels; he calls himself a worm, and not a man, the disgrace of a man and the outcast of a people. These tokens of ignobility belong to the first coming, as those of sublimity to the second, when he shall come no longer as a stone of offence, nor a rock of scandal, but the highest cornerstone, taken up after rejection and exalted to the consummation, and that very rock cut from the mountain in Daniel, which shall break in pieces and grind down the image of the worldly kingdoms. Of which second coming the same Daniel said: And behold, with the clouds of heaven like a son of man one came, and came even to the Ancient of Days, and was present in his sight, and those who stood by led him forward, and to him was given royal power, and all the nations of the earth according to their kind and all glory shall serve him, and his power is eternal, which shall not be taken away, and his kingdom which shall not be corrupted. Then, of course, he shall have a form honourable and a beauty unfailing beyond the sons of men — for, fair in beauty beyond the sons of men. Grace is poured, he says, upon your lips, therefore God has blessed you forever. Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most mighty, in your fairness and beauty — when the Father afterwards, having made him a little lower than the angels, crowned him with glory and honour, and put all things under his feet. And then they shall know him, whom they pierced, and shall beat their breasts tribe to tribe — namely, because in the past they did not recognize him, set in the lowliness of the human condition. Jeremiah says: He is a man, and who shall know him? Because, says Isaiah, his birth too, who shall declare? So too in Zechariah, in his person — nay, even in the mystery of his very name — Christ, the truest priest of the Father, is delineated by a twofold dress for his two comings. First he is clothed in filthy garments — that is, in the indignity of passible and mortal flesh, when the devil too opposed him, namely the author of Judas the betrayer, who had even tempted him after his baptism. Then, stripped of his former filth, he is adorned with the robe to the feet and the mitre and the clean turban — that is, of the second coming; since he is shown to have attained glory and honour. Nor will you be able to call him the son of Jehozadak, who was in no way clothed in a filthy garment, but was always adorned with the priestly robe, nor ever deprived of the priestly office. But this Jesus is the Christ, high priest of God the Father most high, who at his first coming came in human form and passible, in humility, even to the passion, himself made a victim through all things for all of us, who after his resurrection, clothed in the robe to the feet, was named priest forever of God the Father. For thus I will give the interpretation of the two goats too, which were offered at the fast. Do not they also show the twofold order of the name of Christ, who has now come? Equal indeed and alike on account of the same appearance of the Lord, since he is to come in no other form, as one who has to be recognized by those by whom he was also injured. But one of them, wrapped in scarlet, cursed and spat upon and rent and pricked, was cast out by the people outside the city into perdition, marked with the plain emblems of Christ's passion — who, wrapped in a scarlet robe and spat upon and afflicted with every insult, was crucified outside the city. But the other, offered for the offences and given as food only to the priests of the temple, marked the tokens of the second representation, by which, all offences expiated, the priests of the spiritual temple — that is, of the church — should enjoy, as it were by a kind of feast, of the Lord's grace, while the rest fasted from salvation. Therefore, since the first coming was sung both obscured by very many figures and laid low with every dishonour, but the second both manifest and worthy of God, for this reason — looking only to the one they could easily both understand and believe, that is, the second, which is in honour and glory — they were not without cause deceived concerning the more obscure, the more unworthy, surely, that is, the first. And so to this day they deny that their Christ has come, because he did not come in sublimity, while they are ignorant that he was first to come in humility. Let it suffice thus far to have run through the order of Christ on these matters for the present, by which he is proved to be such as he was announced, so that now, from this consonance of the divine Scriptures, we may understand also that the things foretold as to come after Christ are, by the divine disposition, believed to be struck out. For unless he had come after whom they had to be struck out, by no means would the things have come to pass which were foretold as to happen at his coming. Therefore, if you see all the nations emerging thereafter from the depth of human error toward God the creator and his Christ (which you do not dare to deny was prophesied, since, even if you denied it, at once in the psalms, as we have already said, the promise of the Father would confront you, saying: You are my Son, today I have begotten you, ask of me and I will give you the nations for your inheritance and the ends of the earth for your possession), you will not be able to claim Solomon, David's son, for this prophecy rather than Christ, the Son of God, nor that the ends of the earth were promised to David's son, who reigned within Judaea alone, rather than to Christ the Son of God, who has now illumined the whole world with the rays of his gospel. In short, the throne forever fits Christ the Son of God rather than Solomon, a temporal king, of course, who reigned over Israel alone. For today the nations call upon Christ, who did not know him, and the peoples today take refuge in Christ, whom they once knew not. You cannot contend that to be future which you see come to pass. Either deny that these things were prophesied, when they are seen before your eyes, or that they are fulfilled, when they are read; or, if you deny neither, they will be fulfilled in the one in whom they were prophesied.
